I need to implement mentions in text messages. So when i tap @ there should be a list of members in the group, and when i start typing, the ones should be included, like a search. And when the message is sent, the mentions should be clickable and on click it open the user profile.
This is how element x handles it.
Triggering the Mention List
The @ character triggers user mentions, # triggers room mentions. The detection happens in two places:

Plain text composer: CompletionSuggestionService.swift uses a regex /[@#]\S*/ — when the cursor is within a match that starts with @ or #, it fires a SuggestionTrigger.

Rich text editor (WYSIWYG): The WysiwygComposer library handles it internally and publishes a suggestionPattern which is converted to the same SuggestionTrigger type in ComposerToolbarViewModel.swift.

The text after @ (e.g. @jo → "jo") is used to filter room members by user ID or display name (case-insensitive).

Extracting Mentions from a Sent Message
Plain text mode — mentions are stored as NSAttributedString attributes (.MatrixUserID, .MatrixRoomAlias, .link). When sending, the composer enumerates all .link attributes, finds their associated mention attributes, and converts them to markdown: [DisplayName](matrix.to/#/@user:server). The user IDs are collected into PlainComposerContent.mentionedUserIDs.

Rich text (WYSIWYG) mode — the WysiwygComposer tracks mentions internally. When sending, wysiwygViewModel.getMentionsState() returns a MentionsState which is converted to IntentionalMentions (a struct with userIDs: Set<String> and atRoom: Bool).

Both paths ultimately produce an IntentionalMentions which is sent as the Mentions Rust struct via the Matrix SDK — see IntentionalMentions.swift.
